evals.prompt: Create a new ASP.NET Core MVC app called Acme.Web and wire it to Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. Generate strongly typed models for it, but don't invent any pages from the content model yet - I just want the plumbing in place.
evals.expected_output: A solution with an MVC project from the standard template on an installed stable SDK; Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore from the current package line (release candidates installed with --prerelease); a local tool manifest at .config/dotnet-tools.json pinning Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator; generated models in a dedicated directory; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs through the builder callback (delivery.Options.BindConfiguration); tag helpers registered, AddKontentRichText called and ImageTransformationOptions bound with a ResponsiveWidths ladder in appsettings.json; an AGENTS.md carrying the Kontent.ai conventions section with the real generated directory and regeneration command; a .gitignore; a green build; and no controllers, views or routes derived from content types.
assertions: A .config/dotnet-tools.json manifest pins Kontent.Ai.ModelGenerator

All ten content types of the environment were generated (Article, BlogPost, CallToAction, Disclaimer, Event, LandingPage, Page, Person, Service, Video), each carrying the auto-generated header and a [ContentTypeCodename] attribute

The web project references Kontent.Ai.Delivery, Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration and Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore from one package line (the current release-candidate line unless the user or framework forces the previous stable one)

Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form, AddDeliveryClient(delivery => delivery.Options.BindConfiguration("DeliveryOptions")) or equivalent, not an IConfiguration or Action<DeliveryOptions> overload
_ViewImports.cshtml contains @addTagHelper *, Kontent.Ai.AspNetCore
Program.cs calls AddKontentRichText and binds ImageTransformationOptions, and appsettings.json has an ImageTransformationOptions section with ResponsiveWidths
AGENTS.md exists at the root with a Kontent.ai section that states generated records are DTOs mapped to view models through mappers, names the generated directory and gives the regeneration command
No controller, view or route was created for a content type
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

The environment is public, so no key was invented: tracked configuration contains no PreviewApiKey or SecureAccessApiKey entry at all, not even an empty placeholder, and UseSecureAccess/UsePreviewApi are false

evals.prompt: Add Kontent.ai Delivery to the existing MVC solution in existing-net10-cpm (Acme.slnx) using environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. Keep our target framework and central package management exactly as they are.
evals.expected_output: Kontent.ai packages added as PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props with version-less PackageReference items in Acme.Web.csproj; TargetFramework unchanged; models generated into the web project; DeliveryOptions bound in Program.cs; a green build; and no edits to files unrelated to the integration.
assertions: Acme.Web.csproj still targets net10.0
Directory.Packages.props contains PackageVersion entries for every Kontent.ai package added
No PackageReference in Acme.Web.csproj carries an inline Version attribute
Generated models exist in a dedicated directory inside the web project and compile

Program.cs registers the client with the builder callback form, AddDeliveryClient(delivery => delivery.Options.BindConfiguration("DeliveryOptions")) or equivalent, not an IConfiguration or Action<DeliveryOptions> overload
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report
No controller, route, view model or content view was added, and the only pre-existing file edited besides the project and configuration files is _ViewImports.cshtml
No AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md was created or edited in the existing solution; the report proposes the conventions section instead
Every Kontent.ai package resolves from one major line, and that line targets the project's framework
Files edited in the existing solution keep their original line endings and byte-order mark

evals.prompt: Scaffold a Kontent.ai MVC app for environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019 and then implement a listing page and a detail page for the Article content type. Keep the Delivery DTO handling out of the controllers, and render the article body rich text and the article image with the Kontent.ai ASP.NET Core helpers.
evals.expected_output: A working vertical slice: a content service that owns IDeliveryClient queries and maps to view models, a thin controller that returns NotFound for a missing item, Razor views using the rich-text and img-asset tag helpers, typed queries with the request cancellation token, a green build, and no global navigation or site structure invented beyond the article pages.
assertions: A service or similar class depends on IDeliveryClient and builds the Article queries; no IDeliveryResult, IDeliveryItemListingResponse or Pagination type escapes it, and no controller references IDeliveryClient
A mapper per content type (IAsyncMapper or IMapper over IContentItem<T>) produces the view models, and the article view model exposes ItemId, IRichTextContent and IAsset
The detail query passes the request CancellationToken to ExecuteAsync
A slug that matches no article makes the controller return NotFound(), and a failed Delivery result is both logged and surfaced as an error rather than rendered as empty content
The listing query uses GetItems<Article>() with element projection and OrderByElement via the generated codename constants
The detail view renders the body with a rich-text tag helper rather than raw HTML output
The article image asset is rendered with an img-asset tag helper
No navigation menu, homepage composition or routes for content types other than Article were invented
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report
The rendered article detail page contains no missing-resolver HTML comment, so any component embedded in the body has a registered resolver

evals.prompt: Build the whole website represented by this Kontent.ai environment: 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that navigation, URL hierarchy and page composition cannot be derived from content-type names, inspects the environment enough to propose a bounded first slice (or asks which routable type to implement), and does not silently generate a site map, menu and routes for every content type.
assertions: The response names specific evidence from the environment for why the site cannot be inferred, such as content types without a URL slug or section pages with no link to the items they would list
The agent either asks the user which content type to start with or recommends one specific bounded first slice
No navigation menu or URL hierarchy spanning multiple content types was generated without confirmation
A compiling Kontent.ai integration was still delivered: the packages are referenced, DeliveryOptions is bound, and the content types are generated
The solution builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it rather than by the run's own report

evals.prompt: Generate the MVC integration for our secured Kontent.ai environment <environment-id>. I've exported the Secure Access key as KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY in this shell - use it, but make sure it never ends up in the repo, in a command, or in your summary.
evals.expected_output: Requires a real Secure Access environment; replace <environment-id> and export KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY before running. The agent checks the variable is present without printing it, passes it to the model generator and to user-secrets by variable reference only, enables UseSecureAccess in tracked configuration, and neither prints nor commits the key.
assertions: The Secure Access key value does not appear in any file under the output directory
The Secure Access key value does not appear in the agent's final report or in any command it ran; commands reference $KONTENT_SECURE_ACCESS_KEY by name
The model generator was invoked with --DeliveryOptions:UseSecureAccess true and the key passed by variable reference
The application stores SecureAccessApiKey in user secrets or reads it from an environment variable, and UseSecureAccess is true in the tracked DeliveryOptions section
dotnet build completes with zero errors

evals.prompt: Add the latest Kontent.ai MVC integration to the Legacy.Web app in existing-net8, environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019. It's on net8.0 and we can't move it right now.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that the current Kontent.ai packages target net10.0 only, and stops rather than working around it: no Kontent.ai package or tool is installed, the app is not retargeted, and nothing is left half-integrated. The report names the incompatibility, says the previous 19.x line is not a supported path for this integration, notes that .NET 8 reaches end of support in November 2026, and puts the framework upgrade to the user as an explicit choice.
assertions: Legacy.Web.csproj still targets net8.0 and no target framework was changed anywhere
No Kontent.Ai.* PackageReference was added to any project file, and no .config/dotnet-tools.json was created
The report states that the current Kontent.ai packages require net10.0, citing the restore incompatibility rather than asserting it
The report puts the framework upgrade to the user as a decision instead of making it, and does not present Delivery 19.x as a supported fallback for this integration
The existing app is left in its original working state: the fixture still builds with zero errors and zero warnings, verified by the grader building it

evals.prompt: Create a React frontend with an ASP.NET Core BFF that reads content from Kontent.ai environment 8a80c10d-3530-016a-4222-675cc7ba3019.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises that this skill targets server-rendered MVC and does not apply the Razor recipe: no Razor views or tag helpers for content rendering, and a clear statement that the BFF/SPA architecture needs a different approach (it may still set up the Delivery client for an API project).
assertions: The response states that server-rendered MVC with Razor is the wrong shape for this request and says where the presentation boundary goes instead
Rich text and assets are resolved server-side into the API contract rather than left as raw Delivery payloads for the client to interpret
If any Delivery client registration was produced, it uses the builder callback form of AddDeliveryClient

evals.prompt: The content model changed - regenerate the Kontent.ai models in the Acme.Web app in regenerate-net10 and make sure nothing stale is left behind.
evals.expected_output: Models regenerated with the manifest-pinned local tool, the environment ID read from the app's own DeliveryOptions. Three content types no longer exist in the environment. Two of them, Brewer and Cafe, are referenced by nothing, so their records are deleted. The third, Coffee, is used by Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs, so the agent leaves both that file and Coffee.cs alone and reports the situation for the user to decide: the content type is gone, this file depends on it, and the query will return nothing. Article regains the topics element the checked-in copy was missing. The app still builds.
assertions: The environment ID came from the app's own DeliveryOptions configuration, not from a guess or an unrelated sample environment
Brewer.cs and Cafe.cs are gone: both are content types the environment does not have and nothing in the app references them
Coffee.cs is still present, because Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs depends on it, and the app still builds with zero errors, verified by the grader building it
Acme.Web/Services/ProductFeed.cs is unchanged: the agent did not delete or rewrite the user's code to resolve the situation on its own
The report states that the coffee content type no longer exists in the environment and names ProductFeed.cs as the file that depends on it, leaving the decision to the user
Article.cs regained the topics element that the checked-in copy was missing, both the TopicsCodename constant and the Topics property, which only a real regeneration produces
The regeneration used the tool version pinned in .config/dotnet-tools.json rather than a global install or a different version
The report separates what was removed, what was added and what was deliberately left in place, rather than describing the change in general terms
